items.english: Outside the now-dark door, a violent sound of rain and wind — a {t:storm}.
notes: Kept frame bare and unadorned as first of three linked storm appearances; no verb added beyond perception.

sentences: いつか暗くなった戸の外に、激しい雨風の音がする、嵐だ。

items.english: The father and mother and child had gathered at the {t:table} under the dark {t:electric-light} hanging against the wall of the narrow room, about to have supper. Father and mother were both still really young. And the child was a chubby, round baby girl, just able to stand holding on to the {t:table}.
notes: 親子 rendered as father and mother and child to keep both parents present for p2-s2; table kept as same word for grab-hold anchor.
Dark kept outside {t:electric-light} token so period dim bulb stays.

sentences: 親子は、狭い部屋の壁際にぶらさがった、暗い電燈の下の卓に集まって、今夕食をしようとしてゐた。
まだ本当に父も母も若かった。
そして子供は漸測卓につかまって、立ってる事が出来る程の、くり々と肥ってる女の子だった。

items.english: Neither the man nor the woman had yet a single wrinkle in the face. But in the shade of his thick eyebrows his hollowed, kind-looking eyes showed a weary colour of tiredness. And in her dark hair and about her slight shoulders could be seen a still deeper, sunken tiredness, and a drowsy {t:rest}.
notes: Kept tiredness repeated, not varied; drowsy kept distinct from tired for まどろむ / 打沈んだ; {t:rest} for 安らかさ as recurring chord, not calm.

sentences: 男も女も、その顔にはまだ少しの皺もよってなかった。
しかし男の濃い眉毛の陰のくぼんだ優しさうな瞳には、だるさうな疲れの色が見えてゐた。
そして女の濃い髪のいろや、細やかな肩のあたりには、なほ打沈んだやうな深い疲れと、まどろむやうな安らかさとが見えてゐた。

items.english: The day had ended. The grief and suffering of that day were about to flow into the {t:rest} of night. And they smiled in silence, fixing their eyes on everything in the child.
notes: Smile kept as smile for 微笑 to hold thread to table laughter and vision; they left as noun to avoid resolving to parents by pronoun alone, per referent map.

sentences: 一日が終ったのであった。
その日の悲しみも苦しみも、夜の安らかさに流れやうとしてゐるのだった。
そして、彼等は黙って微笑しながら、その子供のすべてに瞳を注いだ。

items.english: Standing unsteadily, the child with fat, round, ball-like short hands tried without a moment's pause, and far too fast, to sweep everything off the top of the {t:table}. So, smiling, they put all the rice bowls and the teapot and the aluminum pots and the rest under the {t:table}. On top of the {t:table} there was left only the small spoon the child held and a single small plate.
notes: Kept smiling, not varied, to hold smile network; kept same table word for clearing action that returns later.

sentences: 子供は、あぶなさうに立ちながら、肥えてまるく鞠のやうに短い両手で、すこしのすきまもなく、そしてあまりに早くテーブルの上のものを掻き廋さうとしてゐた。
それで彼等は微笑みみながら、すべて茶碗や土瓶、アルミ鍋などを、テーブルの下に置いた。
テーブルの上には、わづか子供の持つ小さなスプーンと小皿が一枚残されたばかりであった。

items.english: But the child gave a noisy cry, full of small joy, and banged the spoon and the plate down on the {t:table}.
notes: Kept noisy cry, not laugh, to preserve 叫声 distinct from smile thread.

sentences: けれども子供は、さわがしい、小さなよろこびに満ちた叫声を上げて、スプーンと皿をテーブルの上にたゝきつけた。

data.say: Drafted p1-p6 in spare close voice, keeping storm, table, rest and smile repetitions linked for the later fall into distance.
